title: Blues unpopular in Harlem; Dixieland giving way to stomp-era jazz
summary: He says blues singers were not popular, that Prohibition-era bands used racks of effects, and that bands were growing to seven and eight men with arrangements.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: But how did you, for instance, in Harlem in 1923, with a band, how did you look on the blues singers?

1- 13th century German singers
2 early medieval wandering minstrels.
Was it primitive music to you?
Blues singers were not very popular in Harlem.
But a lot of musicians have told me they felt that was kind of simple-minded music.
It lacked the sophistication. Is that how you looked on it, too?
Well, yes I wanted music like, like—this was a new period coming in. And the period like, "King Porter's Stomp". And it was the beginning of jazz. Before that it was Dixieland.

But now, you see what had happened when prohibition set in, the people were looking for something. And then all that time, something to stimulate them. Those that didn't go to the different drugs and to become alchoholic, you know?

So, what did they do. The drummer first had a big rack up. And he had tin pans and everything on this rack. The trumpet player had a whole lot of different mutes and the derbys and that. To make queer sounds. It was more cacophony than it was actually music.

So now we come to the age, we just beginning to butt out into the age of the Stomp and real jazz. Because before that it was Dixieland. When I was in Baron's, and when I left Atlantic City, it was Dixieland style. // But now, Dixieland was giving way, and such bands like, you know, some of the fellas from Ohio and Fletcher Henderson and my band and some of the other bands. Sammy, uh, the Ten Dark Knights -- we all played -- getting a little above Dixieland now, getting out of the five and six man band, and we're moving into seven and eight man band.
Where you had to have arrangements.
Yeah, right. Where you had to have arrangements. And like, when you have two men in there, you begin to think about two and three saxophones.
